subject: Careers
title: Problems, feedback and mistakes / My work-ready check
focus: Problems, feedback and mistakes / My work-ready check
objective_verbatim: I can respond to feedback without giving up and choose a sensible next step after a mistake.
I can rate my work-readiness and choose one skill to improve before work experience or transition.
outcomes_verbatim: I can respond to feedback without giving up and choose a sensible next step after a mistake.
I can rate my work-readiness and choose one skill to improve before work experience or transition.
calendar_note: Year A. Spring 2 Week 5, 2027-03-22 to 2027-03-25. Tuesday 23 March 2027, Tuesday P3. One 40-minute lesson. Spring 2 runs 22 February to Thursday 25 March 2027. Week 5 is four days with no Friday; the Tuesday lesson is unaffected.

outcomes_verbatim: I can respond to feedback without giving up and choose a sensible next step after a mistake.
I can rate my work-readiness and choose one skill to improve before work experience or transition.
sources.note: The current brief supplies the exact focuses, outcomes and row mapping. Other scheme columns are not asserted verbatim. Activities and 40-minute sequencing are newly authored in the accepted Spring 1 format.
Read for file shape, timing, tiers, feedback, private response and typed/scribed access conventions.
Read for the six-outcome closing Evidence Sheet grid pattern. Current six outcomes are rows 22–27 and current Week 5 combines rows 26–27.

source_adaptation: Exact owner-supplied focus and outcomes retained. Rows 26 and 27 share the closing Week 5 lesson. Newly authored invented workplace practice, not a quotation of absent sequence/evidence columns.
timing: Recall one helpful work habit from earlier weeks. Explain that a rating is a private starting point, not a grade.
Pre-teach feedback and rate. Model scenario A and a rating supported by an invented work clue. Explain that asking for help can show resilience.
Work through B; use main hinge and parallel recheck. Check a sample work clue against a skill without giving a class rank.
First 5 minutes C response and next step. Next 7 minutes six-skill self-rating and one skill/action/support/check plan. Keep evidence distinctions clear.
Private feedback and reply. Bank actual work. Complete six exact-outcome grid from earlier evidence and today's response. Missing earlier work stays not yet seen.
timing_basis: Accepted Spring 1 Careers format: 5 + 8 + 10 + 12 + 5 = 40. Processing time and short pauses sit inside the total. Slides marked same task time share the 12-minute independent block.

routes.Supported: Use C. Pick a calm reply from two choices. Pick a safe next step. For the work check, point to a rating and choose one skill with an adult. The adult records your words and help.
routes.Independent: Use C. Give a calm reply, a fix and a check for next time. Rate the six skills using work you kept. Pick one skill and one small step to practise.
routes.Aspire: Use C and D. Explain when to ask for help or stop for safety. Use a work clue to explain your rating. Say how you will know your small step has helped.

cases.title: Scene 1
cases.situation: In a made-up packing room, a worker puts a box on the wrong shelf. A team leader says, 'Check the shelf label first.'
cases.question: What could the worker say and do next?
cases.answer: Thank you. Please show me the right shelf. Then check the label and move the box with help if needed.
cases.reason: They listen, ask what to do and use the feedback to put it right.

cases.title: Scene 2
cases.situation: In a made-up cafe, a worker has put cups in the wrong place. A colleague says, 'These go on the low shelf.'
cases.question: Choose: ask which shelf, or leave the task and never try again. What should happen next?
cases.answer: Ask which shelf, then put the cups there if it is safe.
cases.reason: A short question helps the worker fix the error and try again.

cases.title: Scene 3
cases.situation: In a made-up garden store, a worker misses one plant while watering. The team leader says, 'Check each pot before you stop.'
cases.question: Give a calm reply. Choose one step to fix the mistake and one way to check next time. Choose a reply: Thank you. I will check the pots. / I will hide the mistake and stop. Choose a step: Water the missed plant as taught and check each pot. / Leave it and say nothing.
cases.answer: Thank you. I will check the pots. Water the missed plant as instructed, then check each pot before finishing.
cases.reason: The worker responds to feedback and uses a simple check to avoid the same error.

cases.title: Scene 4
cases.situation: In a made-up stockroom, a worker hears, 'Put the heavy box up high.' The worker cannot lift it safely.
cases.question: Must they carry on to show effort? Choose a safe reply.
cases.answer: No. Say, 'I need help to move this safely.' Stop and ask the responsible adult or team leader.
cases.reason: Resilience includes asking for help and keeping safe. It does not mean obeying an unsafe request.

worked_example_and_fade.situation: A worker puts a box on the wrong shelf.
worked_example_and_fade.model: Pause. Listen. Say, 'Thank you. Which shelf is right?' Check the label. Move the box safely.
worked_example_and_fade.fade: Model A in full. For B supply only 'Pause. Listen.' For C keep the word bank but leave the reply and next step to the learner.

adaptations.Cognition and Learning: One scenario at a time; retain A and short pause-listen-ask-try-check cue. Offer two choices and read exact outcomes aloud.
adaptations.Communication and Interaction: Accept pointing, communication aid, exact scribe or typed words. Give processing time and a private reply.
adaptations.SEMH: Fictional errors only; no public ranking or demand for personal mistake stories. A planned pause and supported return are valid.
adaptations.Sensory and Physical: Large text; pointing instead of moving cards; position materials for access; never practise an unsafe lift.
adaptations.EAL: Plan in any language. Pre-teach feedback, mistake, rate and next step using the examples.

ta_focus.I Do: Point to the calm reply and safe fix. Model the first step.
ta_focus.We Do: Wait for the learner's choice before reading back. Log any supplied answer.
ta_focus.You Do: Record the pupil's own reply and skill choice, usual access, answer prompts and evidence reference.

prompt_ladder: 1 Point to the place or instruction. 2 Ask a short question. 3 Rephrase the instruction. 4 Provide a scaffold or choice. 5 Model the first step only, then return the task.

main_hinge.question: A worker is told a label is wrong. What is a useful next step?

options.A: Hide the label and stop trying.
options.B: Ask what needs to change, then check and fix it.

main_hinge.decision: If the reply is unsafe or unclear, reread A, model a calm question and recheck with the parallel item before C.

parallel_hinge.question: The task has one error. What could the worker do?

options.A: Ask for help, fix the error and check again.

success: I can choose a useful next step.
I can ask for help if I need it.
evidence_prompts: Small step support and check time

evidence.description: Actual book/typed/pointed/oral response with date, work reference, access, supplied answers, first response, one NS and reply.

assessment: Record actual evidence against each outcome. Shown means evidence covers it with access logged. Partly means some parts shown. Not yet seen includes missing work or a pass; specify which. Do not count an adult model as independent work. Classroom practice is not proof of workplace competence.
private_help_route: Ask a trusted adult for a private talk. Point to HELP, write or use your aid. You may pass, pause and return with help. No personal story is needed.
typed_and_scribed_routes: Book, pointing, an aid, typing or an exact scribe are valid. Read back a scribed reply and allow a change. Record access apart from supplied answers. Plan in any language.

typed_route.heading: Type instead
typed_route.save: Use the usual save routine with lesson code and work reference; share privately.

feedback: VF verbal feedback; WS worked with support; I independent; NS next step; // self-edit; ? read back; E actual evidence saved; R responded. R follows Voice and Audience, one NS and the pupil reply in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. Add to Careers Portfolio. Offer to the Communication portfolio.
where_this_leads: This helps me use feedback and plan one skill to practise before a new work task.
colour_blind_safe: Words and card IDs carry meaning. No colour-only codes.
accreditation: Evidence may contribute to the unit award. Staff confirm actual evidence and mapping; completion is not automatic.
worked_examples_status: All workers, workplace situations and replies are invented. No employer, brand, place or private individual is named.
publication: Only Public replacements and Shared_Resources are intended for public use. Delivery publishes nothing.

Tuesday 23 March 2027 · P3 · 40 minutes · Year A
BUILD Careers · Spring 2 Week 5 · Public edition
Problems, feedback and mistakes / My work-ready check
Unit: Resilience & Change — Work-ready resilience
Theme: Resilience & Change. Five teaching weeks. Week 5 is the closing lesson and brings rows 26 and 27 together. Group: up to five learners. Supported is the default.
Exact lesson outcomes
I can respond to feedback without giving up and choose a sensible next step after a mistake.
I can rate my work-readiness and choose one skill to improve before work experience or transition.
Source: BUILD Careers scheme, Spring 2 rows 26, 27. Focus and outcomes supplied verbatim in the current brief.
Prepare and purpose

Teach useful habits with invented, unnamed workplaces. Books, pens, Support Cards, Vocabulary Mat and Evidence Sheet. Print cards as reusable references. No write-on pupil sheets, internet, login or personal phone is needed. Read the exact outcome aloud and explain the short goal.
Where this leads: This helps me use feedback and plan one skill to practise before a new work task.
Thread tags: SMSC S/So; British Values IL/MR. Respectful speech, a private choice of response and safe help-seeking are practised.
Forty minute sequence

table: Point to one helpful work habit.
Watch A. Pause. Listen. Ask. Try. Check.
Choose a reply and safe fix for B.
Use C. Then rate your skills and pick one small step.
Show one work clue and one skill to practise.

blocks_in_document_order.paragraph: Teaching and checks
Arrival and retrieval 5 minutes
Recall one helpful work habit from earlier weeks. Explain that a rating is a private starting point, not a grade.
I Do 8 minutes
Pre-teach feedback and rate. Model scenario A and a rating supported by an invented work clue. Explain that asking for help can show resilience.
We Do 10 minutes
Work through B; use main hinge and parallel recheck. Check a sample work clue against a skill without giving a class rank.
You Do 12 minutes
First 5 minutes C response and next step. Next 7 minutes six-skill self-rating and one skill/action/support/check plan. Keep evidence distinctions clear.
Review and exit 5 minutes
Private feedback and reply. Bank actual work. Complete six exact-outcome grid from earlier evidence and today's response. Missing earlier work stays not yet seen.
Model and fade
Pause. Listen. Say, 'Thank you. Which shelf is right?' Check the label. Move the box safely.
Model A in full. For B supply only 'Pause. Listen.' For C keep the word bank but leave the reply and next step to the learner.
Hinge and parallel recheck
Main: A worker is told a label is wrong. What is a useful next step? A: Hide the label and stop trying.  B: Ask what needs to change, then check and fix it. Key B.
Parallel: The task has one error. What could the worker do? A: Ask for help, fix the error and check again.  B: Keep the error secret. Key A.
If the reply is unsafe or unclear, reread A, model a calm question and recheck with the parallel item before C.
Access evidence and feedback
Supported
Use C. Pick a calm reply from two choices. Pick a safe next step. For the work check, point to a rating and choose one skill with an adult. The adult records your words and help.
Independent
Use C. Give a calm reply, a fix and a check for next time. Rate the six skills using work you kept. Pick one skill and one small step to practise.
Aspire
Use C and D. Explain when to ask for help or stop for safety. Use a work clue to explain your rating. Say how you will know your small step has helped.
Planned adaptations
Cognition and Learning: One scenario at a time; retain A and short pause-listen-ask-try-check cue. Offer two choices and read exact outcomes aloud.
Communication and Interaction: Accept pointing, communication aid, exact scribe or typed words. Give processing time and a private reply.
SEMH: Fictional errors only; no public ranking or demand for personal mistake stories. A planned pause and supported return are valid.
Sensory and Physical: Large text; pointing instead of moving cards; position materials for access; never practise an unsafe lift.
EAL: Plan in any language. Pre-teach feedback, mistake, rate and next step using the examples.
Prompt ladder and adult focus

Model and card answers
All workplace cases are invented. Accept equivalent safe language. Do not require a public performance or a personal history.
Card A
Thank you. Please show me the right shelf. Then check the label and move the box with help if needed.
They listen, ask what to do and use the feedback to put it right.
Card B
Ask which shelf, then put the cups there if it is safe.
A short question helps the worker fix the error and try again.
Card C
Thank you. I will check the pots. Water the missed plant as instructed, then check each pot before finishing.
The worker responds to feedback and uses a simple check to avoid the same error.
Card D
No. Say, 'I need help to move this safely.' Stop and ask the responsible adult or team leader.
Resilience includes asking for help and keeping safe. It does not mean obeying an unsafe request.
Worked example and fade
Pause. Listen. Say, 'Thank you. Which shelf is right?' Check the label. Move the box safely.
Fade only answer cues; keep reading and communication access.
Judgement and safe delivery
Main hinge
A worker is told a label is wrong. What is a useful next step? A: Hide the label and stop trying.  B: Ask what needs to change, then check and fix it. Key B.
Parallel hinge
The task has one error. What could the worker do? A: Ask for help, fix the error and check again.  B: Keep the error secret. Key A.
If the reply is unsafe or unclear, reread A, model a calm question and recheck with the parallel item before C.
What to retain

Calm response to feedback; Sensible fix after a mistake; Check for next time; Chosen skill and work clue; Small step support and check time. Record the actual words or selections, first attempt, work reference, usual access, supplied choices and answers, one NS and reply. Spelling and handwriting are not the target.
Common errors
A mistake does not mean the worker must give up. A safe pause or help request can be a useful next step. Effort never requires an unsafe task.

The closing grid has six outcomes across five lessons. Rate self-readiness privately, then choose one specific skill and small improvement step with support and a check time. A confident rating is not proof of competence. Missing earlier evidence stays visible.
